Ca and K data are only available for the 1994 wet season, not 1995 dry season

Ambient CO2 seasonal averages were ~364-369 ppm - this is the control
Elevated CO2 treatments are ambient+200 and ambient+300 (two levels of elevation)
Do NOT confuse the two elevated CO2 levels (+200 and +300) with each other
Protein concentration DECREASES with both elevated CO2 and elevated temperature - consistent with dilution effect hypothesis
The Ca and K values in Table 4 appear very low (0.08-0.09% Ca, 0.22-0.24% K) suggesting these are grain mineral concentrations
No Fe, Zn, Mg, Mn, Cu, or other micronutrient data are reported
A typhoon during the 1994 wet season disrupted CO2/temperature control for 72 hours during grain filling - this may affect data quality for that season

recon.extraction_guidance: For meta-analysis of mineral dilution effect: (1) Only Table 4 contains relevant mineral data (Ca, K, protein). (2) CRITICAL: Table 4 reports MARGINAL MEANS only - CO2 columns are averaged over both temperature treatments, and temperature columns are averaged over all three CO2 levels. There are no individual cell means for CO2 x temperature combinations in Table 4. (3) For CO2 effect on minerals: use 'Ambient CO2' column as control and '+200' or '+300' columns as treatment from Table 4 (these are means averaged over both temperatures). (4) Ca and K are only reported for 1994 wet season. (5) Protein is reported for both seasons separately. (6) No SE or SD values are provided in Table 4 - only significance indicators (* or ns). (7) The paper does not report raw cell means for Ca and K at each CO2 x temperature combination, limiting precision of extraction. (8) Extract Ca (0.09% ambient, 0.09% +200, 0.08% +300, ns for CO2) and K (0.24% ambient, 0.22% +200, 0.23% +300, ns for CO2) for 1994 wet season. (9) Protein significantly decreases with elevated CO2 in both seasons (10.0→10.1→9.3% for wet season; 9.3→9.2→8.4% for dry season, averaged over temperatures). (10) No variance data available for Table 4 entries - this limits meta-analysis use.
